cards.title: What Microsoft Word is — and why every office uses it
cards.takeaway: Microsoft Word is a writing app for creating neat letters, CVs, reports, proposals, and flyers ready to print or share.
cards.body:
Think of **Microsoft Word** as clean paper that never runs out of ink and lets you fix any typo in one second.

Businesses, schools, churches, and freelancers use Word every day to create:
- Job CVs and application letters
- Invoices, receipts, and contracts
- Reports, church programmes, and handouts

cards.title: Tour of the Word screen — 5 places to know
cards.takeaway: Title Bar shows the file name, Ribbon holds all tool tabs, Document Area is your paper, and Status Bar counts your words.
cards.body:
When you open a blank document in Word, five parts surround your page:
- **Title Bar (very top):** Shows the file name (starts as *Document1* until you save it).
- **Quick Access Toolbar (top-left):** Tiny one-click icons for **Save**, **Undo**, and **Redo**.
- **The Ribbon & Tabs:** Strips like **File**, **Home**, **Insert**, and **Layout** holding your formatting buttons.
- **Document Area:** The white sheet where you type.
- **Status Bar (very bottom):** Shows page count, word count, and the zoom slider.

check.prompt: Which strip near the top of Microsoft Word holds tabs like Home, Insert, and Layout with all your formatting buttons?
check.hint: It stretches across the top right below the Title Bar and organizes buttons into tabs.
check.explanation: That's it! The Ribbon organizes all of Word's tools into clear tabs like Home, Insert, and Layout.

cards.title: Typing smoothly & fixing mistakes fast
cards.takeaway: Let Word wrap lines automatically; only press Enter for a new paragraph, and press Ctrl + Z whenever you make a mistake.
cards.body:
Typing in Word is much easier than an old typewriter:
- **Word wrap:** Keep typing at the end of a line — Word moves to the next line automatically.
- **Enter:** Press only when you want to start a **new paragraph**.
- **Backspace** deletes to the left; **Delete** removes to the right.
- **`Ctrl + Z` (Undo):** Your magic safety net! Made a mistake or deleted a whole paragraph by accident? Press `Ctrl + Z` and it comes right back.

cards.title: Saving your work early (`Ctrl + S`) — never keep 'Document1'
cards.takeaway: Save in the first two minutes with a clear name in a real folder, then press Ctrl + S every few minutes so power cuts never erase your work.
cards.body:
If light goes off or a laptop battery dies before you save, unsaved typing disappears!

Follow the **2-Minute Save Habit**:
1. Press **`Ctrl + S`** as soon as you start a document.
2. Choose a clear folder (like `Documents/Clients`), **not** a messy Desktop.
3. Give it a real name like `Adaeze_CV_2026.docx` — **never** leave it named `Document1`!
4. Tap **`Ctrl + S`** every few paragraphs to update your saved copy.

check.prompt: What does the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + S do, and why is saving as 'Document1' on the Desktop a bad habit?

choices.text: It shuts down the PC; Document1 uses too much battery
It saves your file; 'Document1' tells nobody what is inside when you have 20 files later
It checks spelling; Desktop files delete themselves at midnight
It prints the page; Word blocks the name Document1

check.hint: Imagine searching for an urgent CV next month when ten files are all named Document1, Document2...
check.explanation: Exactly! Ctrl + S saves your progress instantly, and a descriptive name in a proper folder means you can find the right file in seconds.

cards.title: Making headings and key words stand out (Home tab)
cards.takeaway: Select the text first, then use Bold (Ctrl+B), font size, or alignment on the Home tab so your page is easy to scan.
cards.body:
In Word, the golden rule of formatting is **Select first, then click the tool**:
- Drag across words (or double-click a word) to highlight them.
- **`Ctrl + B` (Bold):** Makes titles and totals strong.
- **`Ctrl + I` (Italic)** & **`Ctrl + U` (Underline):** Add gentle emphasis.
- **Bullets & Numbering:** Turn messy lists into clean steps.

cards.title: Why professionals export to PDF before sending
cards.takeaway: Keep .docx for editing, and export a .pdf copy to send to clients or employers so your layout never shifts on their phone.
cards.body:
Have you ever opened someone's `.docx` file on a phone and seen lines jump to the wrong page? That happens when their phone lacks your font.

**Exporting to PDF (`File → Save As` or `Export → PDF`)** solves this:
- Your fonts, spacing, and page breaks stay **locked** identically on every phone and computer.
- People cannot accidentally type over your CV or invoice.
- Always keep your `.docx` master copy for future edits, and send the `.pdf`!

check.prompt: Why should you export a CV or invoice to PDF before sending it on WhatsApp or email?

choices.text: So the layout, fonts, and spacing stay identical on every device and aren't edited by mistake
Because WhatsApp refuses to send .docx files
Because PDF files automatically translate English into French
So you can never edit your own CV again

check.hint: Think about how fonts and margins behave on different phones.
check.explanation: Spot on! A PDF freezes your exact layout so every employer or client sees the clean page you designed.

cards.title: Essential Word shortcuts worth keeping in your fingers
cards.takeaway: Four shortcuts — Ctrl+S (Save), Ctrl+Z (Undo), Ctrl+C (Copy), and Ctrl+V (Paste) — save hours every week.
cards.body:
Practise these four combinations until they feel automatic:
- **`Ctrl + S`** — Save right now
- **`Ctrl + Z`** — Undo last mistake
- **`Ctrl + C`** — Copy selected text
- **`Ctrl + V`** — Paste copied text

cards.title: Computer froze before you saved? Check AutoRecover!
cards.takeaway: Reopen Word right away and check the Document Recovery panel on the left, then turn on AutoSave / frequent AutoRecover.
cards.body:
If a friend loses a page after a crash:
1. Reopen Word immediately — look at the **Document Recovery** pane on the left for an auto-saved draft.
2. Check `File → Info → Manage Document → Recover Unsaved Documents`.
3. From today onward, save at the very start (`Ctrl + S`) so **AutoRecover** protects you every few minutes!

check.prompt: A friend typed a full page without saving once, and the PC went off. What habit prevents this pain next time?

choices.text: Only type one sentence per day
Save the file with a clear name right at the start and press Ctrl + S every few minutes
Export to PDF before typing any words

check.hint: Saving early gives the file a home on disk and lets Ctrl + S update it in half a second.
check.explanation: Exactly right! Naming and saving in the first minute — plus quick Ctrl + S taps — keeps your work safe from any power cut.
